basis: Heat is the average of the code-computed growth rates available between the two most recent complete years: papers (OpenAlex works with the exact topic phrase in title or abstract) and patent publications (Google Patents where a saved result exists, otherwise EPO OPS, the European Patent Office's worldwide database; topic terms in title or abstract; each topic names its source, and the two count differently, so compare growth, not totals); when patents have not been counted for a topic, heat is the paper growth alone and is marked 'papers only'. Papers so far this year are also compared with the SAME dates last year (the last 30 days left out of both, for indexing delay), so a topic that is fading in the current year loses heat immediately and is marked 'cooling'. It measures how much more is being written and filed about a topic, not whether it is a good investment. Patent counts for recent years are undercounted (publication delay); the current partial year is excluded. Topics with fewer than 20 papers or patents in the earlier year are shown but not ranked (growth from a tiny base is noise). No model is involved.
